etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English ȝellen, yellen, from Old English ġiellan, from Proto-Germanic *gellaną. Cognate with Saterland Frisian gälje (“to yell”), Dutch gillen (“to yell”), German Low German gellen (“to yell”), German gellen (“to yell”).

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To shout; holler; make a loud sound with the voice.
(informal, followed by at) To tell someone off in a loud and angry manner.

quote.text: After the dinner a general reception was held in the spacious parlors of the hotel during which the occasion was very much enlivened with the old college songs and old college yells, which transported us all in mind and feelings […]

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Scots yeld (“ceasing to give milk”).
